newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes pare losses late, light grades steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes pare losses late, light grades steady.

text.p: U.S. crudes pared losses in late trade with light, sweet domestics resilient due to still poor arbitrage economics, traders said on Wednesday.
The fall in delivered Brent for the U.S. Gulf did not immediately cut down prices for Louisiana grades, but traders said they expected pressure to intensify.
"Sellers are marking down their numbers for foreign crude and the arbitrage is far from working," a Midwest trader said, noting only a modest downturn in Louisiana.
But he said Canadian imports and supplies from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) could dampen domestics.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $24.30-40 a barrel, up 20 cents from the previous day.
The Dec/Jan WTI spread held nearly unchanged at 35 cts, keeping WTI/Cushing Posting Plus mostly range-bound at postings plus $2.08-2.12 a barrel.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was moderately active trading between WTI plus 65 to 68 cents a barrel, down a tad from Tuesday's 71-72 cents premium.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire treaded water for a while but recovered to WTI plus 75 cents, up about five cents, with demand still helping to keep differentials buoyant.
Heavy sours began to drift lower with Eugene Island down five cents from Tuesday at WTI minus $1.12 a barrel.
West Texas Sour/Midland was done at a $1.49 and $1.48 discount to the benchmark, facing more pressure from Canadian imports and upcoming SPR sales, traders said.
